title: Microloan Group Guarantee Collapses
scenario: Ngozi Adeyemi, a field officer for a microfinance cooperative in southeastern Nigeria, supervises a solidarity group of eight market women who jointly guarantee each other's loans. One member, Chidinma, has vanished after her stall burned down, leaving a balance the other seven must cover under the contract. Several of them are barely breaking even, and one is feeding orphaned grandchildren. Ngozi's branch is under pressure to keep repayment rates above ninety-five percent, or the cooperative's funding line will be reviewed next month. She must decide how to handle the shortfall this week.
options: Enforce the joint-guarantee clause as written, collecting equal shares from the seven women, because the contract was understood by everyone and the cooperative's survival serves thousands of borrowers.
Quietly cover the shortfall from her own savings and a small discretionary fund, accepting personal financial strain and possible disciplinary action for bypassing procedure.
Report the fire honestly to head office and request a write-off, risking the branch's funding review and her own standing to spare the seven women.

title: The Pensioner's Reverse Mortgage
scenario: Hendrik Vos is a mortgage adviser at a small Dutch lender who earns commission on each product placed. A seventy-nine-year-old widow, Mevrouw de Graaf, asks about a home-equity release so she can pay for private nursing at home rather than move to a care facility. Her children, who live abroad, would inherit far less if she signs. The product is legal and suits her stated goal, but a cheaper municipal care subsidy might partly cover her needs if she navigates a slow application. She wants a decision today because her carer's contract ends Friday.
options: Explain both routes, then proceed with the equity release she explicitly requests, respecting her right to spend her own asset on staying in her home.
Insist she wait for the municipal subsidy decision and consult her children before he will process anything, even though this delays care and she may feel patronised.
Process the application but disclose fully that he earns commission and recommend an independent adviser review, accepting she may take the business elsewhere.

title: Payday Lender's Rollover Algorithm
scenario: Priya Raghunathan is a data scientist at a payday lender serving shift workers across Texas. Her model predicts which borrowers will be unable to repay on the due date and will therefore roll over the loan, paying another fee. These borrowers generate about forty percent of profit. Her manager asks her to refine the model so that collections and rollover offers reach those borrowers earlier. Priya knows the same model could instead flag them for a cheaper installment product, which the company offers but promotes little. Release is scheduled for the quarter's end, and the team's bonuses depend on revenue targets.
options: Build the model as requested; rollovers are disclosed, legal, and chosen by adults who otherwise would lack any short-term credit.
Use the predictions to route likely strugglers to the installment product, accepting reduced revenue and possible conflict with her manager.
Build it as asked but formally document the harm risk to compliance and propose a pilot of the alternative routing, letting leadership decide.

title: A Dowry Loan in Rajasthan
scenario: Kishan Meena, a village moneylender in rural Rajasthan, is asked by the Solanki family for a large loan to fund their daughter's wedding. Dowry is illegal but still expected, and refusing the family would leave the girl's marriage in doubt. Kishan charges high interest, as is customary, but the family's land would be collateral. If the harvest fails, they could lose it. Kishan knows his funds are limited and that two other families have also asked this season. He is respected locally and has never been accused of cheating anyone, yet he must answer the Solankis tonight.
options: Lend at his usual rate with the land as collateral, since the family wants the loan and no formal lender will serve them.
Lend at a much lower rate without land collateral, reducing his own profit and leaving less money for the other two families.
Decline, explaining that he will not finance an illegal dowry, even though the family may then borrow from a harsher lender.

title: Student Debt Collector's Quota
scenario: Tomasz Wrona works in the collections department of a Polish company that purchased a portfolio of old student-loan debts at a deep discount. He is calling Alicja, a thirty-four-year-old nurse who has just returned from unpaid leave after a miscarriage. The debt is legally valid but the statute of limitations may have expired in a way she is unlikely to know. Tomasz's team is paid by recoveries, and a partial payment commitment on this call would meet his monthly target. Alicja sounds fragile and tells him she will pay whatever he asks if it ends the calls.
options: Accept her offered payment arrangement, since the debt is legitimately owed and he is employed to collect it within the law.
Tell her plainly about the possible limitation defense and her right to seek advice before agreeing to anything, forfeiting this month's target.
End the call without commitment, flag her file for hardship review, and let a supervisor decide whether to continue collection.

title: Forgiving a Brother's Loan
scenario: Amara Okonkwo-Reyes lent her younger brother Diego the equivalent of eight thousand euros to open a bicycle shop in Valencia. Two years on, the shop is failing, he has not repaid anything, and he has also taken a second loan from their widowed mother using the same promises. Amara has just received a tax bill and needs the money to avoid penalties; her own family is stable but not wealthy. Their mother's sleep is already troubled by worry. A cousin has warned that Diego is gambling the shop's takings. Amara must decide how to approach him before the family gathering this weekend.
options: Formally demand repayment with a deadline, treating the debt as a real obligation regardless of family ties.
Forgive her loan entirely and urge him to focus on protecting their mother's money instead, absorbing the financial hit herself.
Confront him about the gambling first and condition any leniency on him seeking help and giving a written repayment schedule to both lenders.

title: Selling the Mortgage Bundle
scenario: Lerato Mokoena is a structured-finance analyst at a Johannesburg bank preparing to package several thousand township home loans into a security for sale to pension funds. Internal reviews show that about one in six loans was originated with income documentation she suspects was inflated by commission-hungry brokers. The risk is disclosed only in general terms in the prospectus. The sale would free capital for new affordable lending and would also earn her a promotion. Her director says the due-diligence standard has been met legally. Pricing closes on Monday morning.
options: Proceed with the sale as structured, trusting the disclosed legal standard and the benefit of recycling capital into new affordable housing loans.
Insist on specific disclosure of the suspected inflated-income loans, even if it delays pricing and jeopardizes the deal and her promotion.
Remove the questionable loans from the pool and keep the rest moving, reducing the volume and the capital freed for new lending.

title: Forgiving Fishermen's Boat Advances
scenario: Captain Bui Thanh Hai runs a fish-buying cooperative on Vietnam's central coast. For years, he has advanced cash to boat crews against future catches, tying them to sell only to him at a fixed price. A typhoon has wrecked three boats, and their crews now owe him more than they could earn in four seasons. Neighboring buyers offer better prices but demand upfront payment. Hai's own margins are thin and he owes a bank. He could write off the debts, restructure them, or enforce repayment through seizing nets and engines. The crews wait outside his office for an answer.
options: Enforce the advances by seizing engines and nets, because his cooperative cannot survive if debts are forgiven whenever disaster strikes.
Restructure the debts with no interest and free the crews to sell wherever they wish, losing his captive supply and risking his own bank loan.
Write off half and keep the exclusive-sale tie until the rest is repaid, balancing his survival against theirs.

title: Student Co-signer Dilemma
scenario: Fatima Al-Mansoori, a bank loan officer in Abu Dhabi, is reviewing an education loan for Yousef, a gifted engineering student from a modest family. His uncle has offered to co-sign, but the uncle's records show he is already guaranteeing two other relatives' loans and could not absorb a default. The uncle insists he is happy to sign. Without this loan, Yousef loses a scholarship-matched university place abroad. Fatima knows an exception to the guarantor rules is possible but would require her to omit a note about the uncle's other obligations. Her branch rewards approvals and tracks defaults loosely.
options: Approve using the uncle as co-signer without highlighting his other guarantees, since he consents freely and the student's future is at stake.
Decline the co-signer and tell the family the loan cannot proceed on this basis, accepting that Yousef may lose his place.
Record the uncle's obligations fully and send the file to credit committee with a recommendation, knowing the committee will probably decline.

title: Debt Relief for a Departing Tenant
scenario: Mrs. Eilidh Campbell, a retired landlord in Glasgow, is owed fourteen months of arrears by a tenant, Darius, a single father who lost his job in a warehouse closure. Eilidh depends on the rental income because her pension is small, and she has her own mortgage on the flat. Darius has found a lower-paid job and offers to pay twenty pounds a week indefinitely. A letting agent advises eviction and legal recovery, which would take months and leave the flat empty. A neighbor says Darius is honest and trying. Eilidh must decide before the next hearing date.
options: Proceed with eviction and recovery action, because her own income and security depend on rent being paid and the law allows it.
Accept the weekly payment plan and keep him as tenant, accepting a long, uncertain recovery and tighter finances herself.
Offer to cancel part of the arrears if he leaves within two months, giving her the flat back and him a reduced debt.

title: The Church Lending Circle
scenario: Pastor Emmanuel Quaye oversees a small Ghanaian congregation's savings fund, which lends members money at modest interest. A respected deacon, Kwabena, has defaulted after his taxi was impounded, and members are murmuring that the fund should seize his house deeds, which he pledged. Another group wants to waive the loan to show Christian charity, but waiving would leave the fund unable to help a widow who needs a medical loan next month. Emmanuel must lead a meeting tomorrow evening and will be expected to make a recommendation that the congregation will largely follow.
options: Recommend enforcing the pledge against the deacon's house, to protect the fund for all members and treat everyone by the same rule.
Recommend forgiving the deacon's loan, upholding mercy even though the fund may be unable to serve others for months.
Recommend a long, interest-free payment plan secured by a lien but no seizure, balancing fairness with mercy while accepting a slower recovery.

title: Buy-Now-Pay-Later Teen Cohort
scenario: Sebastián Ortiz leads product design for a Colombian fintech whose buy-now-pay-later checkout is popular with eighteen-to-twenty-two-year-olds shopping for sneakers and phones. Data show late fees concentrate among a small group who stack several purchases. His team could add a gentle friction screen showing total outstanding balance, which tests suggest would reduce purchases by nine percent. Investors are watching growth, and a competitor has just launched a frictionless version. Sebastián has authority over the checkout flow and must decide this sprint whether to add the screen to everyone or leave it off.
options: Leave the flow frictionless; users are adults, the product is transparent about fees, and competitors will capture the market otherwise.
Add the balance screen for all users, accepting lower growth and pressure from investors to protect vulnerable heavy users.
Show the screen only to users with several open balances, targeting protection while limiting revenue loss, though some will find this intrusive.

title: Sovereign Debt Negotiation
scenario: Dr. Tendai Moyo, finance ministry adviser in a small southern African republic, is negotiating restructuring with foreign bondholders and a bilateral lender. The country spends more on interest than on health and schools, yet default would cut off imports of fuel and medicine for months. A lender offers a deal with modest relief but requires privatising the national water utility. Tendai's minister wants a recommendation by Friday. Critics at home warn of austerity riots, while the creditors warn that the offer will vanish if talks fail. He must advise on which course gives the population the best prospects.
options: Accept the restructuring with privatisation, securing continued imports and market access while the country stabilises.
Reject the deal and announce a temporary suspension of payments, protecting social spending but risking supply shocks and long exclusion from capital markets.
Counter-propose relief tied to growth indicators without privatisation, risking collapse of talks but keeping assets in public hands.

title: Informal Chit Fund Foreman
scenario: Meenakshi Subramanian manages a chit fund in Chennai in which sixty small shopkeepers each contribute monthly and take turns receiving the pooled sum through auction. One member who won last month, a tailor named Raju, has just disclosed that he took the money to pay for his wife's surgery, not for his shop as stated, and cannot keep contributing. Other members would suffer if payments stop, since several are counting on their turn within the year. The fund's rules require expulsion and forfeiture of his deposits for default. Meenakshi must tell the group at Sunday's meeting.
options: Apply the rules strictly: expel Raju and forfeit his deposit, so that fifty-nine others get the payouts they were promised.
Hide the real reason and propose a temporary suspension of his contributions, trusting that the group will tolerate a quiet exception.
Disclose the situation openly and put it to a vote, allowing members to decide whether to share the burden.

title: Forgiving a Foreign Student's Overdraft
scenario: Branch manager Ingrid Solheim in Trondheim finds a large overdraft on the account of Samira, a refugee student whose government grant was misdirected for three months. The overdraft triggers an automatic referral to a debt collector, which would also register a payment remark that could block Samira's residence permit renewal. Ingrid has authority to reverse fees up to a limit, but not the overdraft itself. She could also hold the referral for thirty days by marking a technical error that did not exist. The regional office audits exceptions closely, and a mistake would be traced to her.
options: Let the automated process run, since manipulating records would be dishonest and she cannot know the grant will be fixed.
Mark a technical error to hold the referral for thirty days, protecting Samira's permit at personal risk of discipline.
Escalate openly to the regional office as a hardship case with a written request to pause the referral, accepting it may arrive too late.

title: A Contested Interest-Free Loan
scenario: Hassan Qureshi, an Islamic banking sharia advisor in Karachi, is asked whether a bank may keep a late-payment charge from a borrower who defaulted. Under the bank's interpretation, the charge is given to charity and not kept as income, but the borrower is a small farmer who had a flood and argues he cannot afford it. The head of retail says that waiving it sets a precedent that invites strategic delay by wealthier clients. Hassan's opinion carries weight with the board and with depositors who trust the bank's religious integrity. He must issue the ruling before the quarterly review.
options: Uphold the charge as written, arguing that discipline protects the integrity of the system and the charity it funds.
Rule that the charge be waived for demonstrably flood-affected borrowers, creating a hardship exception that requires proof.
Rule that the charge stand but order the bank to offer these borrowers a rescheduled repayment with no further penalty.

title: Fishing Village Credit Scoring
scenario: Nilufar Rahimova, a volunteer technologist in Tajikistan, built a mobile app letting remittance-dependent families prove creditworthiness through phone-payment histories. A European investor now offers to scale it, but wants access to the behavioral data, including contacts and location, to improve risk models and sell insights. Many users don't fully understand what they consent to. The funding would let thousands of households access loans at half the local moneylender rate. Without it, the app will shut down within months. Nilufar owns the code but depends on this investor for survival and must reply by month's end.
options: Accept the investment with broad data access, since the lower-cost loans help thousands more than privacy risks harm them.
Accept only if data use is limited to credit scoring with clear, simplified consent, even if the investor walks away and the app shuts down.
Decline and seek smaller grants that preserve privacy, accepting that the service may fail and families return to moneylenders.

title: Loan Shark's Daughter Applies
scenario: Rodrigo Santana, an auditor in São Paulo, reviews the loan portfolio of a cooperative bank he serves part-time. He finds that Dona Ivone, a pensioner and the bank's longest-standing customer, has been charged compounding penalties because of a software misconfiguration that has also affected about two hundred other borrowers. Correcting this will require reversing income of roughly four hundred thousand reais and will trigger an embarrassing disclosure to members. The board chair, a friend who got him the appointment, asks him to fix it quietly going forward and not rewrite history. Dona Ivone has asked about her statement twice.
options: Report the error and recommend full refunds to all affected borrowers, even if this embarrasses the board and strains his friendship.
Agree to correct the system going forward and refund only those who complain, limiting the cost and disclosure.
Fix the system, refund customers with the largest overcharges first, and inform the full board in writing so they choose the scope.

title: Barter, Debt and a Failing Farm
scenario: Aroha Parata is an agricultural lender in Waikato who has known the Kingi dairy family for decades. Their milk payout has fallen and their herd has bovine disease, putting them in covenant breach. The bank's policy is to call the loan, which would force a sale of the farm that has been in the family for four generations and employs three local workers. An investor wants the land for forestry conversion. Aroha believes the family could recover in two years with support, but cannot be sure. Her credit manager asks for a recommendation by Thursday.
options: Recommend calling the loan, since the covenant breach is clear and the bank's duty to its depositors outweighs her personal knowledge of the family.
Recommend a two-year standstill with tight monitoring, accepting the risk that the farm worsens and the bank loses more.
Recommend a managed sale to a buyer who will lease back the land to the Kingis, giving them continued livelihood at a loss of ownership.

title: Debt Bondage in a Brick Kiln
scenario: Sunil Thapa, a procurement officer for a Nepalese construction firm, discovers that the brick supplier offering the lowest price keeps workers in debt by advancing wages and charging interest, making it nearly impossible for them to leave. Local law is weakly enforced, and the supplier says the advances are voluntary and customary. Switching to another supplier would raise costs by twenty percent on a government contract with penalty clauses, and may cost the firm its bid margin. The workers' families, if the kiln lost the contract, could lose their housing on site. Sunil must finalise the supplier by tomorrow.
options: Keep the current supplier, since the practice is customary, legal in practice, and cancelling would hurt the same workers it is meant to protect.
Switch to a pricier supplier without debt arrangements, absorbing the cost and risk to the firm's margin on principle.
Keep the supplier but require, as a contract condition, cancelling the debts and paying wages directly, risking the supplier's refusal and a delay.

title: The Wedding Fund Override
scenario: Yuki Tanabe is a credit-union clerk in Osaka who realises that elderly member Mr. Hayashi is withdrawing his savings repeatedly and handing the cash to a man who calls himself a grandson in need. Mr. Hayashi, who is lucid but lonely, insists these are gifts to family and has refused to speak to his actual daughter. The credit union has a discretionary procedure for suspected elder fraud, but using it without his consent would breach confidentiality and could damage his trust. Another large withdrawal request is waiting on her counter right now.
options: Process the withdrawal, respecting his competence and right to give his money as he wishes, and note her concerns in the file.
Delay the withdrawal and contact his daughter and the police under the fraud procedure, overriding his stated wishes to prevent possible loss.
Speak with him privately, share her worry and fraud warning signs, and let him choose, processing the withdrawal if he still insists.

title: Writing Off a Dead Man's Loan
scenario: Beatriz Fuentes, estate officer for a Chilean mutual aid society, learns that a deceased member, Don Aurelio, owed the society a sizeable loan. His widow, Marta, knows nothing of it, and the contract allows the society to claim it from his estate, which consists mainly of the house where she lives. The society's board includes members who believe debts must be honored even after death, or trust erodes. Marta is elderly, and her late husband's pension has ended. Beatriz is responsible for informing her and for recommending a course of action to the board.
options: Inform Marta and pursue the estate claim, since the debt is valid and the society's integrity depends on consistent treatment.
Recommend the board write off the debt in full as a gesture of solidarity, accepting the loss and the precedent it sets.
Inform Marta and propose a small monthly repayment that does not threaten the house, balancing the society's claim with her security.
tension: obligation beyond death vs. present need

title: Unlicensed Lender Seeks Legitimacy
scenario: Mariam Diallo, a legal officer at a Senegalese regulatory agency, meets Boubacar, an unlicensed lender who serves market traders in a district where banks refuse to operate. He charges rates above the legal cap but also lends within hours, with no paperwork, and has never used violence. He offers to register and accept oversight if the agency tolerates his current rates for a year while he builds up capital. Enforcing the cap strictly would close him down and push borrowers toward less scrupulous lenders. Her superior wants a firm line to show the agency is serious.
options: Refuse any tolerance and enforce the cap, since the law protects all borrowers equally and exceptions invite abuse.
Grant a one-year supervised grace period under registration, accepting that some borrowers pay high rates in return for greater oversight and access.
Offer registration with an immediate but gradually decreasing rate cap, risking that he refuses and borrowers lose their lender.

title: Crowdfunded Medical Debt
scenario: Elias Bergström, a Swedish journalist-turned-fundraiser, helped raise funds for a Canadian-based friend, Tara, to pay a hospital debt after a cycling accident. The campaign surpassed its goal, collecting three times what was needed. Tara's debt is cleared and she has recently said she would like to use the surplus to start a small business, as donors gave in good faith to relieve her suffering. Several donors have asked privately whether leftovers will be returned or given to others in similar situations. Elias administers the campaign page and is expected to post a final update tonight.
options: Let Tara keep the entire amount, since the donors gave to help her and she best knows her needs.
Return or redistribute the surplus to donors or to others with medical debt, as that is closest to what contributors intended.
Post an open update offering donors a choice, and send Tara a share to cover lost income, with the remainder to others.
tension: fairness vs. loyalty to a friend

title: A Jubilee for the Fishing Cooperative
scenario: Councillor Malia Faleolo of a Samoan village chairs a committee that holds a revolving fund from a diaspora gift, lending to families for funerals, church levies and boats. Several families are well behind on repayments, while others, equally poor, have paid faithfully with great sacrifice. A visiting aid official suggests a one-time forgiveness 'jubilee' to restart the fund fairly. Those who repaid object that forgiveness rewards defaulters and punishes the dutiful. Faleolo's decision will shape village relations and the fund's future, and she has been asked to propose a resolution at the next fono.
options: Propose forgiving all arrears, resetting the fund and prioritising the village's harmony and future lending capacity.
Propose that all debts remain due, but offer extensions and no penalty, honoring those who paid faithfully by not rewarding non-payment.
Propose forgiveness for defaulters, with a matching credit or gift to those who repaid on time, using remaining fund capital to restore fairness.
tension: fairness to the diligent vs. relief for the struggling
